root_cause.text: The idpf driver unconditionally frees the RSS LUT during soft reset (via `idpf_deinit_rss_lut`) but only reinitializes it when the interface is brought up (in `idpf_vport_open`), leaving a NULL pointer that can be dereferenced by an ethtool command (e.g., `ethtool -x`) if the interface remains down after the reset.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "During soft reset, the RSS LUT is freed and not restored unless the interface is up." The patch removes the unconditional `idpf_deinit_rss_lut(vport)` from `idpf_initiate_soft_reset` and adds a conditional reinitialization only when the reset is due to a queue count change and the LUT was not user-configured. The NULL dereference trace shows `idpf_get_rxfh` accessing a NULL pointer, confirming the issue.

candidates.rationale: Unconditionally frees the RSS LUT during soft reset, making rss_data->rss_lut a dangling pointer that becomes NULL if not reinitialized.
Condition that gates the call to idpf_vport_open; when vport_is_up is false (interface down), the RSS LUT reinitialization is skipped, leaving a NULL pointer.
The call that would reinitialize the RSS LUT; it is only executed when vport_is_up is true, so if the interface remains down the NULL pointer is never fixed.
Inside idpf_vport_open, this check is the only opportunity to reinitialize the RSS LUT after it was freed; if vport_open is not called the pointer stays NULL.
The actual reinitialization of the RSS LUT, only reached when vport_open executes; its absence after a reset with the interface down leaves the table invalid.
Subsequent RSS configuration that assumes rss_lut is non-NULL; if the reinit was skipped, this line (or a later dereference) would access a NULL pointer.
